description: Read the Marketo activity log — what leads actually DID or had done to them (emails sent/delivered, alerts, sales emails, campaign requests, data value changes). Start with since_datetime (ISO-8601) or continue with next_page_token; optional lead_ids (max 30) and activity_type_ids (max 10) filter server-side.
embedding_description: Check what actually happened to a Marketo person after a write — whether an email was sent or delivered, an alert fired, or a campaign ran — by reading the activity history since a given time. This is the verb for verifying the consequences of a merge, update or delete after the fact, and for auditing whether an operation notified any human. Distinct from get_leads, which returns current field values rather than a history of events.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Dict with records (a list of activity items, each carrying activityTypeId, leadId, activityDate and attributes) + row_count + spilled=false inline, OR result_blob_key + row_count + spilled=true when large, plus next_page_token and more_result for continuing the read.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Lead with whether any NOTIFYING activity appeared (send email, email delivered, send alert, send sales email, interesting moment) — that is almost always why the caller asked. Report row_count and group the activities by activityTypeId. If more_result is true, say explicitly that the read is INCOMPLETE and next_page_token must be followed before drawing any conclusion — an empty page with more_result true means keep paging, not 'nothing happened'.
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: Never report 'no notifications were sent' unless more_result is false and the whole token chain has been drained. A partial read is not evidence of silence.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Read the activity log for the configured Marketo instance to verify what a write actually caused.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: marketo.invalid_params: neither since_datetime nor next_page_token was supplied (one is required), or since_datetime was not ISO-8601, or lead_ids exceeded 30 / activity_type_ids exceeded 10 — both are Marketo's own server-side caps. marketo.auth_failed: OAuth credentials rejected. marketo.permission_denied: the API user's Role lacks the Access API permission covering activity reads. marketo.partition_access_denied: the API user isn't assigned to the workspace/partition these leads live in. marketo.rate_limited: API rate limit exceeded.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: marketo.invalid_params: supply since_datetime as a full ISO-8601 instant (e.g. 2026-07-28T00:00:00-07:00) for a fresh read, or pass the next_page_token from the previous page; split lead_ids into batches of 30 and activity_type_ids into batches of 10. marketo.rate_limited: retry after a short delay and continue from the last next_page_token rather than restarting. marketo.permission_denied / marketo.partition_access_denied: run check_setup to see the exact gap and which admin screen fixes it. If activity_type_ids returns nothing you expected, read /rest/v1/activities/types.json — activity type ids are not guaranteed identical across Marketo subscriptions.
